messages:
From: Tom Bradford <tom.bradford@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-support@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:28 -0700
Subject: Production p95 spike after omega3 v3.2 deploy — need rollback?

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency jump in our production traffic shortly after your v3.2 rollout to the omega3 model group (~08:40 PDT). p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s for inference requests that include long context (>1k tokens). Attached is a short screenshot from our side showing the spike (p95_spike_20250514.png).

This is directly impacting live sessions (timeouts at the client). Can you confirm whether this is tied to the v3.2 kernel/quantization change you mentioned in the release notes? If so, please revert us to v3.1 or a fallback variant — we need best-effort restoration within the hour.

Also: we will need clarity on how this will affect our SLA for May and whether Redwood will provide a provisional SLA carveout while you revert.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Bradford
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:28:05 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production p95 spike after omega3 v3.2 deploy — need rollback?

Forwarding Acme's note — they hit a clear p95 spike after our v3.2 push. I pulled metrics from Redwood Console (attached slo-impact-summary.csv) and I can reproduce the tail increase: p95 for long-context requests climbed ~5x starting 08:42 PDT, coincident with canary-to-prod promotion.

Initial triage notes:
- Root cause appears correlated with the attention-kernel change in v3.2 that alters caching/kv eviction thresholds for sequences >1024 tokens.
- Immediate mitigation options: 1) surgical rollback to model-omega3 v3.1 for Acme's production traffic, 2) route Acme to the pre-warmed fallback-variant (omega3-compat-v3.1-fallback) while we patch v3.2.

Ask: Laura, can you authorize a controlled rollback for ACME-3421? I included our rollback_playbook_v2.pdf with step-by-step and rollback checklist. If approved I recommend:
- Rollback window: start within 30 minutes of approval
- Traffic ramp: 0 -> 50% over 5 minutes -> 100% over 15 minutes
- Temporary SLA carveout request (we should ask for a 4 hour provisional window to avoid automatic SLA credit triggers while we act)

I've opened INF-9123 (link below) and attached the playbook and SLO summary. Marking as urgent.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Reliability PM | Redwood Inference
--

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production p95 spike after omega3 v3.2 deploy — need rollback?

Laura / Rishi — I validated the Console traces and replayed a subset of Acme traffic in staging. Findings:
- The regression is reproducible and tied to the new attention-kernel heuristics in v3.2 that change KV retention for long sequences.
- No DB schema or tokenizer changes between v3.1 and v3.2 — rollback is expected to be safe from a compatibility standpoint.
- Warm-up: we must pre-warm the KV caches for the fallback variant (recommend 10 minutes of low-rate traffic) to avoid initial tail spikes.

Checklist confirmation (short answers):
- DB/infra deps: None.
- Cache warm-up: required (10 min warm).
- Verification queries: run the standard perf-smoke and 5 synthetic long-context queries; target p95 < 300ms within 20 minutes.
- State risk: Low (no tokenizer mismatch, no stateful persistence changed).

Generated authorization code: AUTH-ROLL-20250514-02
Proposed carveout: 4 hours from authorization start; recommend we start at 2025-05-14T13:00:00-07:00 to allow ops to prep.

Customer comms (draft):
Hi Tom — we identified a regression introduced in a recent model rollout that affected long-context latency. We will temporarily route your production traffic to the last stable variant (omega3 v3.1) and expect full restoration of p95 within 20 minutes of the cutover. We will follow up with a post-mortem and remediation timeline.

Attaching the relevant excerpts from the rollback_playbook_v2.pdf and the SLO impact snapshot (slo-impact-summary.csv).
